cards.front: Recall a key point about Research Methods (Part 2)
cards.back: Quantitative data: numerical, can be statistically analysed. Qualitative data: descriptive, words rather than numbers. Primary data: collected by the researcher. Secondary data: collected by someone else for a different purpose.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Research Methods (Part 2)
cards.back: Measures of central tendency: Mean (average - affected by outliers), Median (middle value - not affected by outliers), Mode (most common - useful for categorical data). Measures of dispersion: Range (highest minus lowest - simple but affected by outliers), Standard deviation (average distance from the mean - more precise but complex).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Research Methods (Part 2)
cards.back: Data presentation: bar charts (discrete/categorical data), histograms (continuous data, no gaps between bars), scatter graphs (correlations), tables (organised raw data). Choose the presentation method that best represents the data type.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Research Methods (Part 2)
cards.back: Ethical issues: informed consent (participants must agree to take part), deception (misleading participants - only acceptable if justified and debriefed), protection from harm (physical and psychological), privacy (right to confidentiality), right to withdraw (participants can leave at any time).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Research Methods (Part 2)
cards.back: The BPS Code of Conduct sets ethical guidelines for UK psychologists: respect, competence, responsibility, integrity. Ethics committees must approve research before it is conducted. Debriefing is essential when deception has been used.

cards.front: What should you know about psychology exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating data, consider: is the mean appropriate or is it distorted by outliers? Is qualitative data too subjective? Is quantitative data too simplistic? Always justify your choice of statistical measure based on the data distribution.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: If a study has ethical issues, it should not be conducted under any circumstances. Correct: Some ethical issues can be managed rather than eliminated. Deception can be addressed through thorough debriefing. Lack of informed consent can be partially addressed through prior general consent or retrospective consent. AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Research Methods (Part 2) including key definitions, research studies and psychological terminology.

cards.front: Key Studies and Theories in Research Methods (Part 2)
cards.back: Research Methods (Part 2) is a core topic in GCSE Psychology that requires understanding of key studies, theories and research methods. The AQA, OCR and Edexcel specifications all require you to know specific studies in detail, evaluate their methodology, and apply psychological concepts to real-life scenarios. cards.front: Applying Research Methods (Part 2) to Real Life
cards.back: GCSE Psychology requires you to apply psychological understanding of research methods (part 2) to everyday situations. Consider how the theories and studies you have learned about explain real behaviour: How does research methods (part 2) affect people in schools, workplaces, families and communities?
